transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-10 14:00 PT
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Maya Hernandez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lucia Chen (Argent Head of Search), Ethan Moore (Argent ML Eng), Priya Singh (Argent CTO)

Summary (auto):
Argent is evaluating embedding-based reranking to improve precision for their customer support search and to reduce time-to-answer. They currently use a hybrid retrieval pipeline (BM25 + ANN) and have evaluated Pinecone and RedisVector. Priority is latency < 150ms for top-k retrieval, throughput ~200 qps during peak, and strong data isolation. Interested in Redwood Hosted for quick start, Dedicated for cost predictability, and Private for data residency.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros please?
[00:06] Lucia (Argent): Hi, Lucia here, I run search. Ethan and Priya with me.
[00:10] Ethan (Argent): Ethan, ML Eng, I own the embedding pipeline and evals.
[00:14] Priya (Argent): Priya, CTO - interested in infra and security.
[00:19] Maya: Great - Samir is our SE, he'll go deep on architecture and benchmarks.
[00:25] Samir (Redwood): Hi folks, hi - just to set expectations we'll talk about integration patterns, perf, and ops tradeoffs. Feel free to interrupt.

[02:05] Lucia: Quick background - we have a customer support KB ~1.1M docs, index updated weekly. Search is currently BM25 + an ANN index for semantic results, but reranking is ad-hoc and slow. We see many false positives for intent mismatch.
[02:40] Ethan: We use 768-d embeddings from an open model and store vectors in RedisVector currently. Similarity scoring then we rerank top 100 with a cross-encoder, which is costly. Looking to move to an efficient rerank using lightweight models and better candidate retrieval.
[03:15] Samir: Cool. Typical pattern we recommend is a two-stage system: efficient ANN retrieval for candidates then a reranker model or a learned scoring layer. Redwood can serve embeddings, store or push to your vector DB, and we have a hosted embedding endpoint if you want to avoid self-managing models.

[05:00] Priya: Security is huge - can Redwood do VPC peering or on-prem? Data retention, KMS?
[05:12] Maya: Yes. Hosted gets you fastest onboarding but we have Dedicated for reserved GPU pools and Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict residency and customer-managed keys. We'll send SOC2 and KMS docs.

[07:30] Lucia: For throughput - peak 200 qps, 95th p95 under 150ms. Our current Redis-based ANN gives ~80ms but reranker kills latency. So want candidate retrieval fast and rerank less expensive.
[08:05] Samir: If you want 200 qps with p95 <150ms for end-to-end, we suggest ~64-128-d embeddings for candidate retrieval? Wait - that sounds confusing.
[08:20] Ethan: (laughs) we actually tried 256-d and saw better recall but higher storage - curious about quantization.
[08:32] Samir: Right - dimensionality tradeoffs: 768 gives richer signals for reranking and cross-encoders, but for high-throughput candidate retrieval you can use 128 or 256 with asymmetric distance or HNSW optimizations. Also Redwood's runtime supports quantized models and int8/4, which reduces GPU memory for Dedicated or Private.

[10:10] Lucia: How tightly do you integrate with vector DBs? We run Milvus in K8s and have pipelines that write vectors into S3-backed blob store too.
[10:27] Samir: We integrate via push/pull patterns - Redwood can host the embedding model and either push vectors to your DB (Milvus, Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, RedisVector) or we can host the ANN tier as part of Dedicated. Typical pattern: Redwood generates embeddings via API, you persist to your vector DB and use it for recall; for rerank we can serve a lightweight cross-encoder from Dedicated or Hosted. Note: transcription sometimes shows duplicate vendor names, but integrations work the same.

[12:30] Ethan: What about hybrid search? We want BM25 + vector-scoring combined for recall. How do you recommend implementing hybrid scoring and routing?
[12:44] Samir: Two approaches: first, BM25 to get a lexical candidate set, then ANN to expand semantically; second is score fusion - compute both lexical and vector scores and combine with learned weights. For throughput you can precompute lexical features and avoid cross-encoder for most cases; only top-10 hit reranked by a heavier model. Redwood supports routing policies so you can route requests to cheaper models for low-confidence queries.

[15:00] Lucia: Any guidance on dimensionality per use case? We support short tickets (1-3 sentences) and some long KB articles.
[15:12] Samir: Short text often performs well with 384 or 512 dims, but storage and ANN ops change. We recommend testing 256 vs 768; often 256 with a good model plus fine-tuning can hit your recall targets while saving 2-3x in storage and index cost. We'll recommend candidate dims after seeing your sample.

[18:30] Ethan: We're also concerned about reranker model cost - cross-encoders are expensive at scale. Could Redwood run a distilled reranker?
[18:45] Samir: Yes, we support distilled rerankers and FFNN scoring layers. We can provision GPU capacity in Dedicated to run those models with predictable throughput. Also consider caching top reranks per query prefix, Redwood has prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated compute.

[21:00] Priya: On Dedicated vs Hosted - what are the cost tradeoffs and SLAs?
[21:12] Maya: Hosted is usage-based, fast to adopt, but if you have steady high qps Dedicated is cheaper and offers reserved capacity with SLA. Private gets you VPC/on-prem and customer-managed KMS. We'll send a side-by-side with estimated monthly cost at your expected 200 qps and 1.1M docs.

[24:10] Lucia: We have compliance auditors who will ask about audit logs and RBAC. Do you provide per-request audit logs and SAML SSO?
[24:25] Samir: Yes - Dedicated and Private include audit logs, SAML/SSO integrations, and RBAC. Hosted has controls too though for enterprise features there is an add-on. We'll include the docs.

[27:00] Ethan: Latency measurement - how do you measure p95 for candidate retrieval vs rerank? We need reproducible benchmarks.
[27:12] Samir: We'll run two benchmarks: (1) ANN-only recall and latency at various dims and index configs (HNSW params), (2) end-to-end candidate retrieval + rerank with your sample queries. We'll produce p50/p95/p99 percentiles and per-token cost estimates. Can run on Hosted sandbox or Dedicated pilot.

[30:40] Lucia: For vector DB ops - does Redwood recommend operator-managed Milvus or managed Pinecone? We prefer self-hosted for data control but open to managed for support reasons.
[30:54] Samir: If you require strict data residency, self-hosted Milvus or Weaviate in your VPC is good; Redwood can push embeddings to that DB. If you want less ops, managed Pinecone or RedisVector as a service reduces maintenance. Dedicated can host ANN as an internal layer to avoid extra hops.

[34:10] Priya: Any gotchas with index rebuilds when you update KB weekly? We need near real-time updates for certain articles.
[34:22] Samir: For frequent updates we recommend incremental indexing and using a messaging pipeline; we also support asynchronous ingest where Redwood can consume events and update indexes. For large rebuilds use cold/rolling index strategy to avoid spikes.

[37:00] Ethan: Do you support hybrid similarity metrics, like asymmetric distance or dot-product with normalization? Our current Milvus setup uses cosine.

[37:12] Samir: Yes - Redwood runtime and integrations support cosine, dot-product, L2, and custom metric layers. For approximate indexes HNSW with inner-product is common. We'll help pick configs.

[40:00] Lucia: Can we try a benchmark with our 100k sample?
[40:06] Maya: Absolutely. Samir, can we coordinate a benchmark plan?
[40:12] Samir: Yes - I'll draft a plan: ingestion instructions, sample queries, desired metrics, and a schedule. We prefer a week for ingest and a 48-hour run to capture variability.

[42:30] Priya: Regarding encryption - can you support customer-managed keys for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[42:38] Maya: Customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted can integrate with KMS for enterprise tiers. We'll include the KMS/HSM details in the security pack.

[45:00] Lucia: One more on retrieval size - how many candidates should we return to the reranker? We currently do top-100 but that seems overkill.
[45:12] Samir: Top-20 to top-50 often sufficient with a good ANN recall and hybrid lexical boost. Top-100 gives headroom but costs more in reranker compute. We'll evaluate with your sample to find sweet spot.

[47:55] Ethan: Any recommended embedding models? We use an open 768-d model now, would Redwood recommend a smaller distilled embedder?
[48:08] Samir: Model choice depends - sentence-transformers variants at 384 or 256 can be quite good. Redwood's model catalog includes verified performance profiles; we'll propose 2-3 candidates and run A/B.

[50:30] Maya: Quick recap - Redwood to share pricing comparison, security docs, and a benchmark plan. Samir will own benchmark; Maya will send pricing. Argent to share 100k sample and list of priority queries.

[50:50] Lucia: Sounds good, thanks.
[51:00] Priya: We'll review docs and get back on scheduling the deep dive.
[51:10] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items in the next 48 hours.
